response_text:
Looking at this PR carefully, I need to verify the new V2 implementation logic by tracing through specific scenarios, particularly the resource name vs ID handling and the permission semantics.

Let me trace `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`:
- `resourceStore.findByType(server, "Groups", ...)` returns resources of type "Groups" - both the schema resource (name="Groups") and per-group resources (name=groupId).
- Inside the lambda: `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)` where `getId()` returns the resource's database UUID.
- But `hasPermission(String groupId, ...)` does `findByName(server, groupId)` which looks up by name (string), not by database ID (UUID).
- The per-group resource is named with the group's ID (UUID), but `groupResource.getId()` returns the resource's own database UUID - these are different.
- So `findByName` will not find the resource, and the fallback to the schema resource will always apply, breaking per-group filtering.

However, hasPermission(String groupId, ...) does findByName(server, groupId), which looks up the resource by NAME (the group's ID), not by the resource's database UUID. In V2 per-group resources are named with the group ID, but getId() returns the resource's own UUID - these are different. findByName will always return null for these lookups, and hasPermission will fall back to the schema (all-groups) resource for every iteration. Consequences: (1) An admin with VIEW_MEMBERS permission only on a specific group will get an empty granted set, so the user search will not filter by groups and no users will be visible (in V2 mode, testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers and testCanViewUserByManageGroupMembers in the new test class would fail). findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission passes resource UUID where group ID is needed
findings.body: Inside the lambda passed to resourceStore.findByType(), the code calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) and adds groupResource.getId() to the granted set. However, hasPermission(String groupId, ...) does findByName(server, groupId), which looks up the resource by NAME (the group's ID), not by the resource's database UUID. In V2 per-group resources are named with the group ID, but getId() returns the resource's own UUID - these are different. findByName will always return null for these lookups, and hasPermission will fall back to the schema (all-groups) resource for every iteration. Consequences: (1) An admin with VIEW_MEMBERS permission only on a specific group will get an empty granted set, so the user search will not filter by groups and no users will be visible (in V2 mode, testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers and testCanViewUserByManageGroupMembers in the new test class would fail). (2) When the admin has the VIEW_MEMBERS scope on the all-groups schema resource, the granted set is populated with the resource UUIDs instead of group IDs, making the value unusable downstream. The V1 analogue in GroupPermissions correctly passes the Resource object directly and strips the name prefix; the V2 version should use groupResource.getName() both in the hasPermission call and when adding to the granted set.

findings.title: canManage() in V2 treats VIEW permission as sufficient for MANAGE actions
findings.body: canManage() returns true when the caller has either VIEW or MANAGE permission on the all-groups schema resource: return hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE). This means an admin with only VIEW permission on Groups can call requireManage() (no-arg) at GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup and successfully create new top-level groups, even though they explicitly lack MANAGE. This is also inconsistent with canManage(GroupModel group) in the same file (lines 73-80), which only permits MANAGE, not VIEW. In V1, canManage() required only the MANAGE_USERS admin role, so VIEW_USERS-like capabilities were correctly excluded. The docstring was updated to mention VIEW, but the behavior contradicts least-privilege and makes 'has VIEW on all groups' grant more capability than 'has MANAGE on a specific group'. The new testManageAllGroups test grants MANAGE explicitly and therefore does not cover or detect this case.

findings.title: resolveGroup only resolves by ID, not by name/path
findings.body: resolveGroup just calls session.groups().getGroupById(realm, id) and returns null when the group is not found. In contrast, resolveUser additionally falls back to getUserByUsername and resolveClient falls back to getClientByClientId. If the id passed to getOrCreateResource is a group name or path (which can happen if a caller misinterprets the field, or if group representation identifiers evolve), getOrCreateResource will fail with 'Could not map resource object with type [Groups] and id [name]'. While the current code paths pass group.getId() (a UUID), the asymmetry with users and clients is worth a comment or alignment so a future caller is not surprised by the silent null.

findings.title: GroupResource.getManagementPermissions/setManagementPermissionsEnabled will crash if invoked under V2
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2 throws UnsupportedOperationException for isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, viewPermission, managePermission, viewMembersPermission, manageMembersPermission, manageMembershipPermission, and getPermissions. The REST endpoints GroupResource.getManagementPermissions and setManagementPermissionsEnabled (lines 321-365 of GroupResource.java) call these methods after only gating on Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ. If a deployment enables ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 together with (or instead of) V1 such that the endpoint is reachable but mgmt() returns MgmtPermissionsV2, the endpoint will throw UnsupportedOperationException on the first request. The endpoints should at least be gated on Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 being absent (i.e., only callable when V1 is the active mode), or V2 should provide a meaningful non-throwing implementation that returns the resource representation for the V2 resource-type resource.

findings.title: New V2 group permissions behavior is not exercised in V2 mode
findings.body: The five new tests in GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest rely on the V1 path: they create permissions via createPermission/createAllPermission scoped under the FGAP-managed client. If the same test is run with ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 enabled, the implementations in GroupPermissionsV2 (canView, canManage, canViewMembers, canManageMembers, canManageMembership, getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, etc.) will be invoked, and - given the bug in getGroupIdsWithViewPermission - several tests (notably testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers and testCanViewUserByManageGroupMembers, where the search filter depends on UserModel.GROUPS being set from getGroupIdsWithViewPermission) will fail. Add a parallel V2 test class (or a parameterized config that also enables ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2) to cover the new V2 code paths before merging.
